## Attribution

Who produced an artefact and where it came from: `author` linked to an Employee, a free-text `source`, `capturedAt`, and an optional `license` for material from outside the organisation. `summary` joins source and author for list rows.

```ts
import { AttributionField } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/audit/attribution-field';
@field attribution = contains(AttributionField);
```

**Deliberately separate from Trust Metadata.** Attribution is provenance; trust is how far to rely on it. The same screenshot can be attributed to a named analyst and still be `self-asserted` — collapsing the two would make "we know who took this" read as "we believe it", which is the mistake that lets weak evidence pass review.

`source` is free text on purpose: it names a system ("exported from the IdP"), a person, or a place ("photographed on site"). An enum would push every consumer into an `other` bucket by its third audit.

## Example
The contained example attributes a log export to the Score Vendor Risk command, captured 2026-08-20. The `author` link is left unset — a system-generated artefact has a source, not a person, and the field must render correctly in exactly that case.

## Non-goals
Does not weigh the evidence (Trust Metadata). Does not hold the artefact (Proof Field). No chain of custody beyond one capture event — a transfer history would be its own append-only record, like Audit Entry.
